text: Remind them The Text just has the pronoun, but the reference is evidently to the Christians in Crete. to subordinate themselves to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
to slander no one, to be peaceable, gentle, demonstrating true humility to all men.

Because we ourselves were also foolish at one time, disobedient, being deceived, being enslaved to various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, detestable, Hey, there is hope! ‘Detestable’ is repeated from 1:16, so if people who are now regenerated were once that way, then they can be changed; there is a way out, through the Gospel. (Actually in the Text the terms are different, synonyms, but the point is the same.) hating one another. This description is very up-to-date; it fits contemporary society very well. So those who were saved out of that milieu should be gentle with those who are still in it.
But when the kindness of our Savior God and His love toward mankind manifested itself,

He saved us—not because of righteous deeds that we ourselves had done but according to His mercy, by means of the bath of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit, The regenerating and renewing are performed by the Holy Spirit.
whom He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that having been justified by His grace we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

The above is a trustworthy statement and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have trusted in God may be concerned to take the lead in good works. I take that to be the normal meaning of the Text—Christians should take the lead in their communities with projects that are for the common good. These things are good and profitable for mankind. If everyone in the world lived according to Biblical principles it would be a much better place! There would be no need for jails, police departments, armies, rehabilitation centers, most hospitals, etc.

But avoid foolish arguments and genealogies and contentions and disputes about the law, because they are unprofitable and useless. Some people like to argue for the sake of arguing, but the Lord Jesus said we will be judged for every idle word (Mt. 12:36).
Excommunicate a divisive man after a first and second admonition,

knowing that such a person has been perverted The passive voice indicates that the person was perverted by an outside force, in this context presumably by Satan; but he went along with the process, allowed it to happen (or he wouldn’t be ‘self-condemned’). So now he is on Satan’s side, and if he refuses to listen to two warnings, he doesn’t want to change. The next best thing is to excommunicate him, not allow him to work within the community. and is sinning, being self-condemned.
As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to spend the winter there.
Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way without delay, that they may lack nothing.
And let our people also learn to maintain good works, to meet pressing needs, that they not be unfruitful. By meeting the needs of God’s servants we share in the fruit of their labors.

All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in faith. The Text doesn’t have “the” faith, just ‘faith’. Perhaps the reference is to those who have never met Paul, but love him anyway. Grace be with you all. Amen.
